page: Amazon Web Services r3.2xlarge is a memory-optimized third-generation server instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor. This CPU provides 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via hyperthreading, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes a 25 MB L3 cache and supports AVX and AES instructions, though it lacks newer instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX.

The instance is configured with 61.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.62 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 160 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between compute and memory capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1285.69 and a Geekbench single-core score of 726.0. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with stress-ng multi-core reaching 6717.9 and large-block memory read bandwidth at 52.14 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also fall into the average tier, while Redis SET operations and LLM text generation for larger models are weak to poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r3.2xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on legacy hardware, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require modern CPU instruction sets or high single-core speeds. It is best suited for workloads such as caching layers, relational databases with moderate transaction volumes, static web serving, and basic multi-threaded data processing.
